builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Curating Always-Loaded Context for LLM Agents: A Capacitated Assortment Model with Censored Feedback
summary: Replaces append-only growth of always-loaded context files (AGENTS.md and equivalents) with a capacitated selection procedure that keeps only a bounded subset of instructions under a token budget. Costs curator effort or an automated selection loop, instrumentation of per-instruction compliance, and accepts the formal result that removing apparently ignored instructions can inevitably delete helpful ones because feedback on loaded items is observable while absent items are censored. Can fail when compliance attribution to individual instructions is noisy, when token price is misestimated, or when reviewer throughput limits how many add/remove edits can be validated per period.
rationale: This is directly actionable at single-GPU or API scale since it concerns curating a small text artifact rather than training or infrastructure, and its main deliverable, pruning always-loaded context, reduces recurring per-session cost while protecting instruction compliance.
technique: Capacitated assortment model for context file curation

claims.statement: Replaces append-only growth of always-loaded context files (AGENTS.md and equivalents) with a capacitated selection procedure that keeps only a bounded subset of instructions under a token budget. Costs curator effort or an automated selection loop, instrumentation of per-instruction compliance, and accepts the formal result that removing apparently ignored instructions can inevitably delete helpful ones because feedback on loaded items is observable while absent items are censored. Can fail when compliance attribution to individual instructions is noisy, when token price is misestimated, or when reviewer throughput limits how many add/remove edits can be validated per period.

The authors prove an upper bound on optimal context-file size independent of the number of candidate instructions, show that appending all positive-value instructions can be arbitrarily worse than optimal subset selection, and report experiments in which irrelevant rules drawn from real context files reduce model compliance; no multiplicative factor is reported in the abstract.
